name: prose-small
description: A small hand-written set of unique prose sentences
samples: The morning light spilled across the kitchen table and made everything look briefly new.
She had always believed that small gestures carried more weight than grand pronouncements.
Rain tapped against the window in a rhythm that matched the old clock on the wall.
He reread the letter three times before he understood what it was really asking.
The garden grew wild that summer, full of weeds and unexpected flowers.
A good story changes the way you see the world even after you forget the details.
They walked to the edge of the field and stood in silence for a long while.
The coffee had gone cold, but neither of them wanted to move to make more.
Every city has a quiet hour just before dawn when it belongs to no one.
She kept the ticket stub in her wallet long after the trip was over.
He learned that patience was not waiting, but deciding not to hurry.
The library smelled of paper and dust and old decisions.
A sudden gust of wind sent the loose pages scattering across the lawn.
They built the boat in the garage over the course of one long winter.
Some questions are worth more than the answers they seem to demand.
The dog waited by the door, hopeful in a way only animals can be.
She wrote her name in the margin of the book, then regretted it immediately.
Evening arrived slowly, as if it was reluctant to commit to ending the day.
He could hear the river from his room most nights when the wind was right.
The best conversations happen when no one is trying to be impressive.
A single lantern hung at the end of the dock, swaying with the tide.
She had rehearsed the apology for a week and still said it all wrong.
The old farmhouse leaned slightly to one side, having long given up on being straight.
He counted the stars until his neck ached and then gave up somewhere past a hundred.
There is a particular loneliness that comes from being understood too quickly.
The pie crust was a disaster, but the filling made up for it entirely.
They argued about maps even though neither of them had any idea where they were.
Frost painted the window glass with delicate white ferns overnight.
She collected postcards of places she had never been and probably never would go.
The train slowed as it entered the station, sighing like a tired animal.
He found an old photograph of his grandmother and studied it for much longer than he expected.
The smell of bread drifted from the bakery and pulled a whole street toward it.
It is strange how a familiar smell can bring back an entire year in an instant.
They planted the tree on a cloudy day so it would not be shocked by the sun.
She kept switching between saying it was fine and saying it was not, and meant both.
The market on Saturday morning was loud, colorful, and completely impossible to rush through.
He wrote his best ideas down in the dark so he could forget them by daylight.
The river had carved the valley over millennia, patient as only stone can be.
A stranger smiled at her on the bus, and neither of them looked away first.
The snow swallowed the town's sound, leaving only the crunch of boots on the way home.
She had a habit of finishing other people's sentences, which did not endear her to everyone.
The lighthouse beam swept across the water every few seconds, a steady pulse in the dark.
He left the door unlocked that night, though he could not have explained why.
Some promises are made just to see how they feel in your mouth.
The kettle whistled, and with it the whole kitchen seemed to come to life.
They measured the year in seasons, not in days, and so it passed more gently.
She kept the letter unopened, certain that its contents would change things she was not ready to change.
The boy counted the steps from the road to the house until he knew them by heart.
A hawk circled high above the field, patient and patient again.
The piano in the corner was out of tune, but everyone pretended not to notice.
